blocks.text: The module documentation explains that sandbox commands have loopback only and that every network decision belongs to the host Unix-socket proxy. The bridge itself only relays bytes.
blocks.title: Bridge design

blocks.text: NetworkMount identifies the host socket directory and sandbox Python. Proxy helpers remove inherited proxy settings, inject loopback proxy variables, and build the bridge launcher argv.
blocks.title: Network mount and environment

blocks.text: bridge_source reads this file itself so the mounted script is exactly the implementation supplied to the sandbox.
blocks.title: Bridge source packaging

blocks.text: A bounded pool serves each connection in a daemon thread. _relay copies bytes between the loopback client and Unix socket, forwards half-closes, and closes both endpoints.
blocks.title: Socket relay

blocks.text: The script parser requires port, socket, and command arguments. main binds loopback, forks the relay server, closes listener and pipes in the child, and execs the command in the parent.
blocks.title: Script argument parsing and launch

gotchas: Bridge setup failure is fail-open as no network
Script must run with Python 3.8 compatibility
how_it_works: Builds proxy environment variables for loopback TCP
Launches a mounted bridge script with a Unix socket
Relays each client socket to the host proxy
Forks the relay and execs the real command
purpose: Bubblewrap keeps sandbox network namespaces closed; this module routes only loopback proxy traffic through a mounted Unix socket to the host proxy. It also contains a standard-library-only script that forks a relay server and execs the target command.
summary: Provides the sandbox-loopback HTTP proxy bridge and environment/argv helpers for controlled network access.

symbols.summary: Identifies the mounted host bridge directory and sandbox Python executable.
Creates loopback proxy variables with an empty NO_PROXY on purpose.
Copies a sanitized environment and replaces inherited proxy variables.
Builds argv that runs the mounted bridge script before the target shell command.
Relays bytes between one loopback client and the host Unix-socket proxy.
Accepts loopback connections and starts a bounded daemon thread for each relay.

symbols.returns: port, socket path, command tuple or None
symbols.summary: Parses bridge port, Unix socket, and target command arguments.
Starts the relay server and execs the target command, with no-network fallback.

unknowns: Host-side proxy policy is implemented outside this file.
